</span></td>
<td id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">
<span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:155.3pt;">
<span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Decision:</span><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> </span><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-bg-color:#B3FFB3;">Answer</span><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> (Summary Only) </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Router Thought:</span><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> “Summaries do not explicitly state ‘values: X’, but they hint at key points… </span><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Since summaries contain the answer</span><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> (responsibility and compassion), use Summary.” </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">Outcome:</span><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;"> Answered correctly (Accuracy preserved) while skipping </span><math id="S5.T6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo mathsize="0.800em">∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.T6.7.1.5.3.1.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4k tokens of raw retrieval.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Qualitative Case Studies</h3>

<section id="S5.SS5.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.5.1 </span>Case Study: Qualitative Cases</h4>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present two representative cases illustrating how TierMem aligns retrieval granularity with query requirements in Table <a href="#S5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ Retrieve-and-Edit improves consolidation hygiene. ‣ 5.4 Consolidation Over Replay Epochs ‣ 5 Analysis and Ablations ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.
Case 1 requires escalation due to entity loss in summarization, and Case 2 can be answered cheaply from summaries because key semantic evidence is preserved. A broader clustering-based analysis of router decision errors is provided in Section <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Router Error Analysis and Failure Modes ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mitigating compression loss.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When the user query requires a specific entity that is missing from Tier-1 summaries, TierMem escalates and grounds the answer in Tier-2 raw logs, avoiding vague or hallucinated responses.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS1.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Ensuring semantic efficiency.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS1.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When Tier-1 summaries contain semantically sufficient evidence (even if not phrased in the same surface form as the query), the router answers directly, avoiding unnecessary raw retrieval while preserving correctness.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.5.2 </span>Anatomy of Summary-Only Failures and Router Decisions</h4>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To better understand the <em id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">write-before-query</em> barrier and how our router responds to summary insufficiency, we analyze the subset of test queries where the <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Summary-Only</span> system fails.
On LoCoMo (<math id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}1540" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1540</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}1540</annotation></semantics></math>), Summary-Only makes <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">378</span> errors (<span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">24.5%</span>).
These errors expose two structural failure modes of write-time compression:
(i) <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">information is missing</span> from Tier-1 (no recoverable answer span), and
(ii) <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">over-generalization</span> where decisive entities/values are replaced by coarse abstractions (e.g., “Sweden” <math id="S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> “her home country”).
Table <a href="#S5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ Why many errors persist even after escalation. ‣ 5.5.2 Anatomy of Summary-Only Failures and Router Decisions ‣ 5.5 Qualitative Case Studies ‣ 5 Analysis and Ablations ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> summarizes the dominant root causes.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Write-before-query manifests as missing or unrecoverable evidence.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The largest portion of Summary-Only errors (<span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">41.3%</span>) are due to <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">missing information</span>:
the needed answer is not present in the retrieved summaries at inference time.
This is a direct symptom of write-before-query: the memory writer must decide what to keep before knowing the future query, so some decisive constraints/attributes are never preserved in Tier-1 in a query-usable form.
A second major slice (<span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">28.8%</span>) is <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">over-generalization</span>, where summaries retain topic relevance but lose <em id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">answer-critical specificity</em> (entities, modifiers, exact values), making the evidence <em id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">semantically related yet insufficient</em>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Router decisions on Summary-Only failures.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given these 378 Summary-Only errors, our router routes <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">72.0%</span> (272) to <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Escalate</span> (R) and <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">28.0%</span> (106) to <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Answer</span> (S).
However, only <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">10/106</span> (<span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">9.4%</span>) of S decisions are actually justified by summaries containing the gold information;
the remaining <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">96/106</span> are false cache hits where the router should have escalated.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why many errors persist even after escalation.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A key finding is that <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">72.0%</span> of Summary-Only failures are <em id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">already</em> recognized as summary-insufficient (router chooses R), yet the final answer remains wrong.
This indicates that remaining failures are dominated by the <span id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">R-path</span> rather than the routing decision itself:
(i) retrieval may fail to locate the correct raw page,
(ii) the raw evidence may still be missing or already generalized upstream (i.e., the source-of-truth does not contain an explicit answer span in the stored pages), or
(iii) the generator may fail to extract/compose the correct answer even when relevant evidence is present.
This motivates improving <em id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">provenance-guided retrieval quality</em> and <em id="S5.SS5.SSS2.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">grounded answer extraction</em> in addition to improving the router.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 7: </span><span id="S5.T7.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Root causes of Summary-Only errors</span> on LoCoMo (<math id="S5.T7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}1540" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1540</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}1540</annotation></semantics></math>; Summary-Only errors <math id="S5.T7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=378" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>378</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=378</annotation></semantics></math>).
The top two categories (missing information and over-generalization) are direct manifestations of the write-before-query barrier.</figcaption>

<td id="S5.T7.9.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;"><span id="S5.T7.9.8.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">33</span></td>
<td id="S5.T7.9.8.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;"><span id="S5.T7.9.8.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">8.7</span></td>
<td id="S5.T7.9.8.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:10.0pt;padding-right:10.0pt;">
<span id="S5.T7.9.8.4.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:345.0pt;">
<span id="S5.T7.9.8.4.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.T7.9.8.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Miscellaneous failures.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>Router Diagnostics on Summary-Only Error Cases</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We further analyze the router system on the same 431 Summary-Only error cases to diagnose whether failures stem from (i) incorrect <em id="S5.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">routing decisions</em> or (ii) limitations in the <span id="S5.SS6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Escalate</span> (raw-grounded) path.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">A large fraction are false cache hits (should escalate but answered from summaries).</h5>

<div id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Among the 431 Summary-Only errors, the router selects <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Answer</span> in <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">191</span> cases (44.3%).
Crucially, <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">148</span> of these are <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">false cache hits</span>—the router answers from Tier-1 although summaries do <em id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">not</em> contain the gold evidence (<span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">34.3%</span> of all 431 error cases).
This indicates that the dominant router failure mode is <em id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">insufficient strictness</em> in sufficiency checking, often triggered by superficial keyword matches that do not verify slot completeness or exactness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Escalation is often triggered correctly but can still fail downstream.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">240</span> cases (55.7%), the router correctly escalates, yet the final answer remains wrong.
This suggests that improvements must also target the <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Escalate</span> pipeline, e.g., ensuring the raw store contains the needed detail, improving provenance-guided retrieval coverage, and strengthening the grounding constraints during generation to avoid falling back to the same generalized phrasing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Connecting back to write-before-query.</h5>

<div id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">These results highlight a two-part mitigation strategy for write-before-query:
(1) <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">reduce lossy abstraction at write time</span> (e.g., entity/number/date retention constraints), and
(2) <span id="S5.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">tighten inference-time sufficiency checks</span> to detect when summaries are merely topically related but lack decisive evidence.
In our setting, (2) is especially urgent, as false cache hits directly harm correctness.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span><span id="S5.T8.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Router behavior on Summary-Only error cases (n=431).</span>

</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Long-horizon LLM agents must remain consistent over histories spanning days to months, yet context windows and inference budgets make feeding full raw logs costly and sometimes ineffective: even with context-extension methods, compute grows with length, and models exhibit position-sensitive degradation on long inputs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
Accordingly, non-parametric agent memory systems rely on external read–write stores to support long-term personalization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yehudai et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Representative approaches include OS-style hierarchical management (MemGPT) and controller-based memory operation (SCM), as well as write-time compression and organization (MemoryBank, Mem0, LightMem) and structured memories such as temporal knowledge graphs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Packer et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhong et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chhikara et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fang et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rasmussen et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
In contrast, TierMem explicitly treats memory access as inference-time evidence granularity allocation: it answers from a cheap, provenance-linked summary tier when sufficient, and escalates to an immutable raw tier only on detected insufficiency, with verified write-back for amortization.
We evaluate this trade-off on long-horizon benchmarks including LoCoMo and LongMemEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maharana et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Agentic Memory Retrieval and Auditable Grounding</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond storage, retrieval in long-term interaction is inherently a control problem: models must decide when and how much to retrieve and when to stop to avoid under/over-retrieval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
Related work studies iterative retrieval and reflection-based improvement, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shinn et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and emphasizes verifiable grounding via retrieve–revise pipelines and fine-grained citations <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cao and Wang, 2024</a>)</cite>.
Closer to agent memory, retrieval controllers such as MemR<sup id="S6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sup">3</sup> and page-store-based deep research systems optimize closed-loop evidence gathering under cost constraints <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Du et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yan et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
In contrast, TierMem collapses control into a cost-sensitive binary routing decision (<span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Answer</span> vs. <span id="S6.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Escalate</span>) across memory granularities, uses provenance pointers to enable auditable fallback to raw pages, and consolidates only verified evidence back to the fast tier.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We identify a structural failure mode in summary-centric long-horizon memory: the <span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">write-before-query</span> barrier, where write-time compression can induce <span id="S7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">unverifiable omissions</span> and break auditability.
To address this, we propose <span id="S7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TierMem</span>, which treats retrieval as <span id="S7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">inference-time evidence allocation</span>: answer from a fast summary tier when evidence is sufficient, and <span id="S7.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Escalate</span> to an immutable raw-log source of truth only when necessary, then write back <em id="S7.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">verified</em> findings with provenance links.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Across <span id="S7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LoCoMo</span> and <span id="S7.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LongMemEval</span>, TierMem improves the accuracy–efficiency tradeo-off, approaching raw-grounded faithfulness while substantially reducing query-time cost.
Analyses further show that (i) a lightweight sufficiency router can reliably control escalation with small overhead, (ii) provenance pointers materially improve escalated grounding quality, and (iii) verified write-back increases cheap-path coverage over time without degrading accuracy.</p>
</div>
</section>

<span class="ltx_bibblock"><span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_author">D. Wu, H. Wang, W. Yu, Y. Zhang, K. Chang, and D. Yu</span>

</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock">External Links: <span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_links"><span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_external">2410.10813</span>,

</span></li>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Implementation Details</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Memory Instantiation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our framework is general; in experiments we instantiate the memory management system using the open-source <span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mem0</span> library <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chhikara et al., 2025</a>)</cite> for vector indexing and storage. We adapt Mem0 to our <span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Paged-Log Architecture</span> as follows:</p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Summarization prompt (<math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\text{summ}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">summ</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\text{summ}}</annotation></semantics></math>).</span>
We replace Mem0’s default entity-graph extraction with <span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">page-level summarization</span>. The prompt instructs the model to generate a concise, self-contained summary of the interaction log, preserving key dates, decisions, and user preferences.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Storage schema.</span>
Each page summary is embedded and indexed in the vector store. We extend Mem0 metadata to include the Page ID (<math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>) as a provenance pointer <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, enabling retrieval to map back from a summary vector to its originating page.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Embedding model.</span>
We embed summaries with <span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">text-embedding-3-small</span>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Mem0 components used vs. disabled.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In our implementation, Mem0 is used only for (i) storing and querying embeddings for Tier-1 summary entries and (ii) attaching/retrieving metadata (e.g., <span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">raw_log_id/page_id</span>) for provenance.
We do not use Mem0’s entity-graph construction, graph updates, or graph-based retrieval; these components are disabled/bypassed so that Tier-1 consists solely of page summaries plus metadata pointers.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Paged-Log Ingestion and Persistence</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement a <span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">paged ingestion</span> procedure that converts streaming dialogue turns into fixed-size <em id="A1.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">pages</em> stored in a persistent <span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PageStore</span>. Each incoming turn is appended to the current page with an explicit timestamp and speaker tag. Once a page reaches a configured maximum length (default: 1000 tokens), we trigger a summarization-and-indexing step via <span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mem0.add(infer=True)</span> over the entire page.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Page format.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each page stores raw interaction text line-by-line in the canonical form:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\text{timestamp}]~\text{speaker}:~\text{text}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mtext>timestamp</mtext><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>speaker</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.608em">:</mo><mtext>text</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\text{timestamp}]~\text{speaker}:~\text{text}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This preserves multi-speaker context for datasets with more than one interlocutor.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Provenance.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each page <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, we generate a unique <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">page_id</span>. We set <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">raw_log_id</span> <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leftarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leftarrow</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">page_id</span> in Mem0 metadata such that any retrieved summary hit can be deterministically mapped back to the original raw page content in <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PageStore</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Durability and replay.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PageStore</span> persists pages to disk and supports session-scoped loading. This enables resuming runs without re-ingesting all prior turns and ensures that the raw evidence used for research-mode grounding remains accessible.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Deferred Summarization for Unindexed Pages</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To handle sessions that terminate before a page fills (or failures during ingestion), we provide a <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">deferred summarization</span> routine <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">auto_summary</span>. It enumerates pages whose summaries have not yet been stored and calls <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mem0.add(infer=True)</span> for each such page. The returned memory strings are recorded in <span id="A1.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PageStore</span> and the page is marked as indexed, ensuring that the vector store remains consistent with the persistent log.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Query Answering Pipeline</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given a query <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, we first retrieve top-<math id="A1.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> summary hits from Mem0 using vector similarity search. Each hit contains a summary text and a provenance pointer to its source page.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Two-path routing (S/R).</h5>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use a lightweight router to select between:</p>
<ul id="A1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">S-path (Summary-only).</span> When retrieved summaries contain an explicit answer, we generate the response directly from the summaries.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">R-path (Research).</span> When summaries are ambiguous or incomplete, we switch to a slower research mode that grounds generation in raw page evidence.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cost accounting.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We record (i) Mem0 retrieval token usage and latency, (ii) router token usage, and (iii) answer-generation token usage. These are aggregated into online cost metrics for analysis.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Research Mode: Integration–Plan Loop </h3>

<div id="A1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The R-path implements an iterative loop that alternates between <span id="A1.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">integration</span> (extracting grounded facts from evidence) and <span id="A1.SS5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">planning</span> (deciding whether to retrieve more evidence).</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evidence construction.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We group retrieved hits by <span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">page_id</span> and build an evidence block that includes:
(i) Mem0 page summaries (when available) and
(ii) the full raw page content from <span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PageStore</span>.
This ensures that research mode always has access to verbatim text for grounding.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Integration step.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The integration prompt extracts a set of <em id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">linked facts</em> of the form:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\texttt{fact},~\texttt{evidence\_quote}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">fact</mtext><mo rspace="0.497em">,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">evidence_quote</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\texttt{fact},~\texttt{evidence\_quote}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Crucially, we <em id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">do not</em> ask the model to generate provenance identifiers.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Deterministic provenance linking.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After integration, we map each extracted fact to its source pages using a deterministic post-processing step:</p>
<ul id="A1.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">First, we attempt substring matching of the normalized <span id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">evidence_quote</span> against each page’s raw content (and, if needed, its summaries).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If quote matching fails, we fall back to keyword overlap between the fact text and page content.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This produces <span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">source_pages</span> and <span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">evidence_snippets</span> without relying on model-generated page identifiers, reducing hallucinated provenance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Planning step.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A separate planning prompt evaluates coverage and returns either <span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">DONE</span> or <span id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">SEARCH</span> with retrieval commands. We support two retrieval operators:</p>
<ul id="A1.I4" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MEM0_SEARCH</span>: semantic retrieval over Mem0 summaries.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">KEYWORD_SEARCH</span>: BM25-style keyword search over raw pages in <span id="A1.I4.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PageStore</span>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A1.SS5.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We deduplicate issued commands and terminate early when no new pages are discovered.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.6 </span>Dynamic Write-back Protocol</h3>

<div id="A1.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We implement online consolidation as a closed-loop memory update step. Given a set of <em id="A1.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">verified</em> linked facts extracted during the Research Integration phase:</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">1. Conflict Retrieval.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each new candidate fact <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{new}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{new}</annotation></semantics></math>, we query <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> to retrieve the top-<math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=3</annotation></semantics></math>) most similar existing summary units, denoted as <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{retrieved}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{retrieved}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">2. Operation Selection.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We prompt an LLM (the <span id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Memory Manager</span>) to compare <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{new}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{new}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{retrieved}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{retrieved}</annotation></semantics></math>. The model outputs one of four actions:</p>
<ul id="A1.I5" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">SKIP</span>: If <math id="A1.I5.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{new}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{new}</annotation></semantics></math> is semantically entailed by <math id="A1.I5.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{retrieved}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{retrieved}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">UPDATE</span>: If <math id="A1.I5.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{new}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{new}</annotation></semantics></math> adds specific details (e.g., timestamps, names) to a vague existing entry. The model generates the merged text.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ADD</span>: If <math id="A1.I5.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{new}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{new}</annotation></semantics></math> represents a distinct, previously unindexed event.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">3. Provenance Inheritance.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If an <span id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">UPDATE</span> occurs, the new unit inherits the provenance pointers <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> from both the original unit and the new evidence sources, maintaining a complete audit trail.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.7 </span>Reranking (Optional)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When enabled, we apply a <span id="A1.SS7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">page-level reranker</span> to candidate evidence pages. Hits are first grouped by <span id="A1.SS7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">page_id</span>; reranking operates on each page’s raw content (or, if missing, concatenated summaries) and selects the top-<math id="A1.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="A1.SS7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unique pages</em>. We also include a <span id="A1.SS7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">protection rule</span>: pages with high-confidence Mem0 similarity scores are retained to avoid discarding highly relevant memories before reranking.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Discussion: Online Consolidation vs. Epoch-wise Replay Evaluation</h5>

<div id="A1.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">TierMem is designed to support <em id="A1.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">online</em> consolidation: after an escalation, verified findings can be written back immediately to reduce future misses.
However, to match the benchmark evaluation protocol and avoid within-run distribution shift, our main experiments report results under an epoch-wise replay setting where Tier-1 is held fixed within each epoch and updates are applied between epochs.
We expect that in interactive deployments, moving write-back into the QA loop is straightforward and may further reduce repeated escalations, but careful design is needed to preserve reproducibility and to avoid unintended interactions with evaluation sampling.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.8 </span>Statistics and Debug Instrumentation</h3>

<div id="A1.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For analysis, we log per-query events including (i) route choice (S vs. R), (ii) hit breakdown by <span id="A1.SS8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">source_type</span> (<span id="A1.SS8.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">original</span> vs. <span id="A1.SS8.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">linked_fact</span>), (iii) linked-fact write-back counts, and (iv) latency/token usage. This instrumentation is used only for evaluation and does not affect the core algorithm.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> TierMem QA (Abstract): Router + Bounded Retrieve–Integrate–Plan Loop</figcaption>

             <span id="alg1.l2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}(Q,Z_{0})=\textsc{Answer}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Answer</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}(Q,Z_{0})=\textsc{Answer}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">then</span>



</div>
<div id="alg1.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
              
              
              <span id="alg1.l3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg1.l3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Gen}(Q,Z_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Gen</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Gen}(Q,Z_{0})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4:</span></span>

<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">

<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Router: Data Construction, Training Pipeline, and Hyperparameters</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix consolidates all details related to router supervision, SFT distillation, GRPO optimization, and the exact hyperparameters used.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Task Definition and Notation</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The router is a lightweight controller that decides whether the system can answer a user query using Tier-1 summaries alone (<span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Answer</span>/S) or must escalate to Tier-2 raw logs (<span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Escalate</span>/R).
Given a query <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> and an initial evidence state <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> consisting of the top-<math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> retrieved Tier-1 summaries, the router predicts:</p>
<table id="A2.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\sim\pi_{\theta}(a\mid Q,Z_{0}),\qquad a\in\{\texttt{S},\texttt{R}\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">S</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">R</mtext><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\sim\pi_{\theta}(a\mid Q,Z_{0}),\qquad a\in\{\texttt{S},\texttt{R}\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The router output is <em id="A2.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">strictly</em> a JSON object with an action token (and optionally a teacher <span id="A2.SS1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">thinking</span> field during distillation).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Data Construction: Summary Sufficiency Labels</h3>

<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Source benchmark slice.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We construct router training data from the <em id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Long-Range Understanding (LRU)</em> competency in MemoryAgentBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, using a summarization-style subset of 2,000 instances. Each instance is materialized into a linked two-tier memory state <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathcal{M}_{S},\mathcal{M}_{R})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathcal{M}_{S},\mathcal{M}_{R})</annotation></semantics></math> using the write path described in §<a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Architecture: Provenance-Linked 2 Tier Memory ‣ 2 The TierMem Framework ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>.
For each query <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math>, Tier-1 dense retrieval returns the initial summary evidence <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> (top-<math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> summaries), which forms the router input.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Two-path execution (Summary vs. Research).</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each query <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math>, we execute two fixed policies to determine whether <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is sufficient:</p>
<ul id="A2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Summary-only (S-path):</span> <math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Y}_{S}\leftarrow\mathrm{Gen}(Q,Z_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>S</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>Gen</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Y}_{S}\leftarrow\mathrm{Gen}(Q,Z_{0})</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Research/raw-grounded (R-path):</span> Run the bounded Deep Search Loop (§<a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Inference Protocol: Adaptive Routing and Consolidation ‣ 2 The TierMem Framework ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>) to obtain <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\mathrm{final}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>final</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\mathrm{final}}</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Y}_{R}\leftarrow\mathrm{Gen}(Q,E_{\mathrm{final}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>Gen</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>final</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Y}_{R}\leftarrow\mathrm{Gen}(Q,E_{\mathrm{final}})</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">LLM judge and sufficiency rubric.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We obtain binary indicators <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{S},c_{R}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{S},c_{R}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> using LLM-based judges with conservative rubrics.
Both judges are run with temperature <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> and are constrained to output a fixed JSON schema to reduce variance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">S-path: summary sufficiency judge.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Q,y^{\star},Z_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Q,y^{\star},Z_{0})</annotation></semantics></math>, the judge determines whether the retrieved summaries contain <em id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">explicitly sufficient</em> information to answer the question correctly <em id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">without guessing</em>.
We use the following prompt (verbatim):</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Judge Prompt for Summary Sufficiency</h3>

<figure id="A2.F2" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A2.F2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="426.8" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 426.8" 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15 403.12)"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" class="ltx_nestedsvg" 20.73 L 253.16 2.95 C 253.16 1.32 251.84 0 250.21 0 L 2.95 0 C 1.32 0 0 1.32 0 2.95 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 11.81 8.38)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:16.59em;--ltx-fo-height:0.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="13.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 10.38)" width="229.54"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Judge Prompt (Summary Sufficiency)</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 15.93)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.91em;--ltx-fo-height:27.28em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.16em;font-size:10pt;" height="379.6" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 377.45)" width="510.73"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.91em;">
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are evaluating whether retrieved summaries contain sufficient information to answer a question.</span></span>
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Question: {question} 
<br class="ltx_break">Gold answer: {gold_answer}</span></span>
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Retrieved summaries: 
<br class="ltx_break">{summaries_text}</span></span>
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Your task:<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Determine if the summaries contain EXPLICIT information to answer the question correctly.</span></span></span>
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Strict criteria (be conservative):<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="A2.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<span id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The answer should be DIRECTLY stated or clearly derivable from the summaries.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Do NOT count vague/related information as sufficient.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="A2.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Do NOT infer causes from effects.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="A2.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For completeness questions (“how many”, “list all”, “both”), summaries must be COMPLETE.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<span id="A2.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For exact details (dates, numbers, names), summaries must contain those exact details.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If you have ANY doubt whether the summaries allow a factual answer without guessing, answer false.<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F2.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output JSON:</span></span><pre id="A2.F2.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
{
  "has_sufficient_info": true/false,
  "reason": "..."
}
</pre>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="A2.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The judge prompt used to evaluate whether the retrieved summaries provide sufficient context to answer the ground truth.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We set <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="c_{S}=\mathbb{I}[\texttt{has\_sufficient\_info}=\texttt{true}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">has_sufficient_info</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">true</mtext><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{S}=\mathbb{I}[\texttt{has\_sufficient\_info}=\texttt{true}]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">R-path: research/correctness judge.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Q,y^{\star},\hat{Y}_{R})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Q,y^{\star},\hat{Y}_{R})</annotation></semantics></math>, the judge determines whether the research-path answer matches the gold answer.
We use a separate LLM-as-judge prompt (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Judge Prompt for Summary Sufficiency ‣ Appendix B Router: Data Construction, Training Pipeline, and Hyperparameters ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>), which outputs a JSON object of the form:
{ ”label”: <span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘‘CORRECT’’</span> / <span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘‘WRON’’</span> }.
We set <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="c_{R}=\mathbb{I}[\texttt{label}=\texttt{``CORRECT''}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">label</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">‘‘CORRECT’’</mtext><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{R}=\mathbb{I}[\texttt{label}=\texttt{``CORRECT''}]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why conservative judging?</h5>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our routing label targets <em id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">summary sufficiency</em>.
False positives (marking summaries as sufficient when they are not) would train a router that under-escalates and produces ungrounded answers.
Therefore, the S-path prompt intentionally biases toward <span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">false</span> when there is ambiguity or missing explicit support.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Routing labels (semantic cache hit/miss).</h5>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We define the router supervision label as:</p>
<table id="A2.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=\begin{cases}\texttt{S}&amp;\text{if }c_{S}=1,\\
\texttt{R}&amp;\text{if }c_{S}=0\land c_{R}=1.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">S</mtext></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">R</mtext></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=\begin{cases}\texttt{S}&amp;\text{if }c_{S}=1,\\
\texttt{R}&amp;\text{if }c_{S}=0\land c_{R}=1.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We drop instances where both policies fail (<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{S}{=}0\land c_{R}{=}0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{S}{=}0\land c_{R}{=}0</annotation></semantics></math>), since they provide no signal on whether escalation can recover missing evidence.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Training Workflow Overview</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train the router using a two-stage pipeline:</p>
<ol id="A2.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stage 1 (SFT / Distillation):</span> Initialize the router to follow the routing protocol and learn strong sufficiency heuristics from a high-capacity teacher (GPT-5) using a strict JSON format.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stage 2 (GRPO):</span> Starting from the SFT checkpoint, refine the decision boundary under an explicit accuracy–cost trade-off, discouraging unnecessary escalation while preserving faithfulness.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This separation is intentional: SFT primarily regularizes behavior and format; GRPO optimizes the accuracy–efficiency trade-off.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5 </span>Stage 1: SFT via GPT-5 Thinking+Action Distillation</h3>

<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Teacher prompt (GPT-5 thinking trace + binary action).</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We distill a teacher-generated <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">thinking</span> trace and the final routing decision <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">action</span> using the following prompt (verbatim):</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.6 </span>Router Thinking Prompt</h3>
