class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="A2.F3.pic1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Router Thinking Prompt</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.24)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.91em;--ltx-fo-height:33.44em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" height="465.14" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 462.68)" width="510.73"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.91em;">
<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are a router for a memory-augmented QA system. Decide whether the retrieved summaries are sufficient to answer the question.</span></span>
<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Available Actions<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="A2.I4" class="ltx_enumerate">
<span id="A2.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="A2.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">“S” — Answer using current summaries only</span><span id="A2.I4.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A2.I4.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Use when: The summaries contain a span that directly states the answer (or a direct paraphrase) WITHOUT needing to assume missing facts. </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A2.I4.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Rules of thumb:</span></span>
<span id="A2.I4.i1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A2.I4.i1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A2.I4.i1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I4.i1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I4.i1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If you can point to a specific snippet that can be copied into the answer, choose S.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="A2.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">“R” — Deep research mode</span><span id="A2.I4.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A2.I4.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Use when: Summaries are too ambiguous, contradictory, or unrelated; OR the question requires a comprehensive list and summaries are clearly incomplete. </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A2.I4.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">R is more reliable than S.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Input<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 
<br class="ltx_break">QUESTION: {question} 
<br class="ltx_break">SUMMARIES: 
<br class="ltx_break">{summaries_block}</span></span></span>
<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Decision checklist<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="A2.I5" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A2.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A2.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">What exact answer format is needed? (single value / list / date / identity)</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A2.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Do summaries explicitly contain it?</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A2.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Any ambiguity or need to infer?</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A2.I5.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A2.I5.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A2.I5.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I5.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Any completeness requirement?</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output (JSON only)<span id="A2.F3.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span><pre id="A2.F3.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
{
  "thinking": "&lt;your reasoning&gt;",
  "action": "S/R"
}
</pre>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="A2.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The updated router prompt incorporating explicit chain-of-thought reasoning to improve decision reliability.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">SFT targets and formatting.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each example, the student router is trained to reproduce the teacher’s JSON response.
We treat the entire JSON (including <span id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">thinking</span> and <span id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">action</span>) as the supervised target, using standard next-token cross-entropy.
At inference time, the system uses only the <span id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">action</span> field.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Teacher-label consistency filter.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure alignment with oracle labels derived in §<a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Data Construction: Summary Sufficiency Labels ‣ Appendix B Router: Data Construction, Training Pipeline, and Hyperparameters ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>, we keep only SFT examples where the teacher action matches the oracle routing label <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>.
Examples with mismatched teacher actions are discarded.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why include thinking in SFT.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The teacher <span id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">thinking</span> field provides structured intermediate reasoning about evidence sufficiency (e.g., completeness, ambiguity, exactness), which improves stability and reduces instruction-following failures (e.g., verbose or malformed outputs) in a small router.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.7 </span>Stage 2: GRPO Alignment for Accuracy–Cost Trade-off</h3>

<div id="A2.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from the SFT checkpoint, we optimize the router with GRPO using a trajectory-level reward:</p>
<table id="A2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(\tau)=R_{\mathrm{acc}}(\tau)\;-\;\lambda_{\mathrm{cost}}R_{\mathrm{cost}}(\tau)\;-\;\lambda_{\mathrm{waste}}R_{\mathrm{waste}}(\tau)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>acc</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>cost</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>cost</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>waste</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>waste</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(\tau)=R_{\mathrm{acc}}(\tau)\;-\;\lambda_{\mathrm{cost}}R_{\mathrm{cost}}(\tau)\;-\;\lambda_{\mathrm{waste}}R_{\mathrm{waste}}(\tau),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where:</p>
<ul id="A2.I6" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.I6.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{acc}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>acc</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{acc}}</annotation></semantics></math> encourages correct routing (choose S when summaries suffice; choose R when escalation is necessary),</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.I6.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{cost}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>cost</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{cost}}</annotation></semantics></math> penalizes choosing R to reflect token/latency overhead,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I6.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I6.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I6.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.I6.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{waste}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>waste</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{waste}}</annotation></semantics></math> penalizes <em id="A2.I6.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unnecessary escalation</em> (choosing R when <math id="A2.I6.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=\texttt{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_monospace">S</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=\texttt{S}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Concrete reward implementation.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In our implementation, rewards are computed from <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(c_{S},c_{R})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(c_{S},c_{R})</annotation></semantics></math> and the router decision <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">GRPO dataset construction.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We build GRPO prompts using the same router input <math id="A2.SS7.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Q,Z_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Q,Z_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> as in SFT. For each prompt, we sample multiple router completions per prompt (generations per prompt is reported in §<a href="#A2.SS9" title="B.9 Hyperparameters ‣ Appendix B Router: Data Construction, Training Pipeline, and Hyperparameters ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.9</span></a>) to compute group-relative advantages.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.8 </span>GRPO Dataset Preparation and Filtering</h3>

<div id="A2.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Starting from the offline QA logs (which include both summary-path and research-path outcomes), we apply the following filters:</p>
<ol id="A2.I7" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I7.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I7.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I7.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Remove instances where <span id="A2.I7.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">both</span> paths fail (<math id="A2.I7.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{S}=0\land c_{R}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{S}=0\land c_{R}=0</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I7.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I7.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I7.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Remove instances where the <span id="A2.I7.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">R-path fails</span> (<math id="A2.I7.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{R}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{R}=0</annotation></semantics></math>), since escalation does not recover evidence.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I7.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A2.I7.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I7.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Optionally re-judge S-path sufficiency using a fixed judge configuration to reduce label noise; keep only instances consistent under re-judging.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS8.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optional augmentation.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS8.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We optionally augment a subset of questions by paraphrasing while preserving intent and specificity (2–3 paraphrases per question). Paraphrases inherit the same memory state and labels.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS8.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Balancing.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To emphasize hard decisions, we oversample cases where escalation is necessary (<math id="A2.SS8.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{S}=0\land c_{R}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>R</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{S}=0\land c_{R}=1</annotation></semantics></math>) during GRPO minibatch formation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS9" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.9 </span>Hyperparameters</h3>

<section id="A2.SS9.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.9.1 </span>SFT Hyperparameters</h4>

<figure id="A2.T9" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A2.T9.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A2.T9.3.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A2.T9.3.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="A2.T9.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Parameter</span></th>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Detailed Analysis of Provenance Pointer Ablation</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix provides a detailed analysis of the provenance pointer ablation study introduced in Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Ablation: Effect of Provenance Pointers ‣ 5 Analysis and Ablations ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>.
We analyze route consistency, accuracy under identical routing decisions, and token-level cost, in order to isolate the effect of provenance-aware warm-start from routing behavior or additional computation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Route Consistency</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Across 1,540 shared queries, Linked and No-Linked make identical routing decisions on 1,306 queries (84.8%), and differ on 234 queries (15.2%).
This indicates that enabling provenance pointers induces only modest changes in routing behavior.
Therefore, improvements observed in the Linked setting cannot be explained solely by more aggressive escalation, but instead suggest higher-quality evidence retrieval during escalation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Accuracy under Identical Routes</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To disentangle retrieval quality from routing effects, we analyze queries where Linked and No-Linked select the same route.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Both Escalate (R).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When both systems escalate to raw logs, Linked answers 31 queries correctly that No-Linked answers incorrectly, whereas the reverse occurs in 25 cases.
This yields a net gain of +6 queries for Linked under identical escalation decisions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Both Answer (S).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When both systems answer directly from summaries, Linked answers 16 queries correctly that No-Linked answers incorrectly, compared to 10 in the opposite direction.
The small difference confirms that provenance pointers primarily affect raw evidence grounding rather than summary-only answering.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These controlled comparisons demonstrate that provenance pointers improve the <em id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">quality</em> of retrieved evidence, independent of routing frequency.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Cost Analysis by Route</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A3.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ C.3 Cost Analysis by Route ‣ Appendix C Detailed Analysis of Provenance Pointer Ablation ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> reports average token usage by route.
On summary-only queries, Linked and No-Linked incur nearly identical cost.
On escalated queries, Linked incurs slightly higher token usage, reflecting deeper or more precise raw evidence grounding.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Importantly, the average research depth is nearly identical between Linked (1.38) and No-Linked (1.36), with the same maximum depth (3), indicating that gains do not stem from additional retrieval iterations.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T12" class="ltx_table">

<section id="A3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.4 </span>Summary</h3>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In summary, provenance pointers consistently improve performance on escalated queries by enabling more reliable raw-log grounding.
The improvement persists under identical routing decisions and does not rely on increased search depth.
While provenance-aware escalation incurs slightly higher token cost, it yields a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off, validating provenance linking as a core component of TierMem.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Additional Analysis: Why Higher Hard-Recall Can Tie on End-to-End Judge Score</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix explains why GPT-4.1-mini achieves higher recall on oracle-hard cases (Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ End-to-end impact. ‣ 5.2 Router Learning and Cost–Fidelity Trade-off ‣ 5 Analysis and Ablations ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>),
yet matches our SFT+GRPO router on the final LoCoMo LLM-as-judge accuracy.
Crucially, this effect does <em id="A4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">not</em> come from different stored memories:
all variants share identical writes and use the same memory library, generator, embedding model, and reranker (cf. evaluation protocol in §<a href="#S4.SS1.SSS1" title="4.1.1 Baselines ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1.1</span></a>).
Instead, the tie arises from how routing interacts with (i) the <em id="A4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">difficulty distribution</em> of escalated queries and
(ii) the <em id="A4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">effective repair/regression behavior</em> of the R-path under the realized evidence trajectories.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>S/R counterfactual comparison matrices on the R-routed set</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each router, we log a counterfactual comparison on the subset of queries routed to R:
we run the S-path answer and the R-path answer and record whether each is correct under the benchmark judge.
This yields a 2<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>2 table with counts:</p>
<ul id="A4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">S_correct_R_correct</span>: both paths would be correct.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">S_correct_R_wrong</span>: R would <em id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">hurt</em> (regression if escalated).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">S_wrong_R_correct</span>: R would <em id="A4.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">fix</em> S (repair benefit).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">S_wrong_R_wrong</span>: both fail (hard negatives).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We report both (i) the raw S/R agreement counts and (ii) their decomposition against the final judge labels (<span id="A4.SS1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">actual_correct/wrong</span>)
to expose how “hard” the routed set is.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">GPT-4.1-mini (R-routed subset).</h5>

<tr id="A4.T13.3.4" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A4.T13.3.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A4.T13.3.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">181</span></td>
<td id="A4.T13.3.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right"><span id="A4.T13.3.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">169 correct / 12 wrong</span></td></tr>

<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Repair benefit vs. regression risk</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Hard-recall is a mechanism metric that measures whether oracle-hard cases are escalated,
but end-to-end judge accuracy depends on whether escalation <em id="A4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">actually repairs</em> S failures without introducing regressions.
From Tables <a href="#A4.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ GPT-4.1-mini (R-routed subset). ‣ D.1 S/R counterfactual comparison matrices on the R-routed set ‣ Appendix D Additional Analysis: Why Higher Hard-Recall Can Tie on End-to-End Judge Score ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>–<a href="#A4.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ Ours (SFT+GRPO) (R-routed subset). ‣ D.1 S/R counterfactual comparison matrices on the R-routed set ‣ Appendix D Additional Analysis: Why Higher Hard-Recall Can Tie on End-to-End Judge Score ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>, we define two diagnostics on the R-routed subset:</p>
<table id="A4.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.E2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{RepairRate}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>RepairRate</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{RepairRate}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\Pr(R\ \text{correct}\mid S\ \text{wrong})=\frac{\text{S\_wrong\_R\_correct}}{\text{S\_wrong\_R\_correct}+\text{S\_wrong\_R\_wrong}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>correct</mtext></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>wrong</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mtext>S_wrong_R_correct</mtext><mrow><mtext>S_wrong_R_correct</mtext><mo>+</mo><mtext>S_wrong_R_wrong</mtext></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\Pr(R\ \text{correct}\mid S\ \text{wrong})=\frac{\text{S\_wrong\_R\_correct}}{\text{S\_wrong\_R\_correct}+\text{S\_wrong\_R\_wrong}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A4.E3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{RegressRate}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>RegressRate</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{RegressRate}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\Pr(R\ \text{wrong}\mid S\ \text{correct})=\frac{\text{S\_correct\_R\_wrong}}{\text{S\_correct\_R\_wrong}+\text{S\_correct\_R\_correct}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>wrong</mtext></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>correct</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mtext>S_correct_R_wrong</mtext><mrow><mtext>S_correct_R_wrong</mtext><mo>+</mo><mtext>S_correct_R_correct</mtext></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\Pr(R\ \text{wrong}\mid S\ \text{correct})=\frac{\text{S\_correct\_R\_wrong}}{\text{S\_correct\_R\_wrong}+\text{S\_correct\_R\_correct}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Measured values.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For GPT-4.1-mini: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{RepairRate}=181/(181+86)=67.8\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>RepairRate</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>181</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>181</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>86</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>67.8</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{RepairRate}=181/(181+86)=67.8\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{RegressRate}=33/(33+240)=12.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>RegressRate</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>33</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>33</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>240</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>12.1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{RegressRate}=33/(33+240)=12.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
For ours: <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{RepairRate}=170/(170+92)=64.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>RepairRate</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>170</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>92</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>64.9</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{RepairRate}=170/(170+92)=64.9\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{RegressRate}=26/(26+313)=7.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>RegressRate</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>26</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>26</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>313</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>7.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{RegressRate}=26/(26+313)=7.7\%</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus, GPT-4.1-mini shows higher repair rate but also higher regression exposure on the set it escalates,
whereas our router is slightly less aggressive in “fixing” but produces fewer cases where R would be worse than S.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Why end-to-end accuracy can tie despite recall differences</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Even with identical writes and identical components, routers induce different <em id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">escalated sets</em> and therefore different
difficulty distributions for the R-path.
This is visible in the <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">hard-negative</span> bucket <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">S_wrong_R_wrong</span>:
GPT-4.1-mini escalates 86 such cases, while ours escalates 92.
Importantly, within this bucket the judge decomposition shows that some instances labeled as <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">S_wrong_R_wrong</span>
still end up as <span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">actual_correct</span> (14 for GPT-4.1-mini vs. 20 for ours), which we interpret as evidence of
<em id="A4.SS3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">trajectory sensitivity</em> in the R-path: small differences in retrieved evidence traces and generation can flip outcomes on extremely difficult instances.
In our runs, the R-path succeeds on more of these hard negatives (20 vs. 14), partially compensating for the lower oracle-hard recall.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Takeaway.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under a fixed write state, the gap between mechanism metrics (e.g., oracle-hard recall) and outcome metrics (judge accuracy)
can be explained by (i) different escalated-set difficulty, (ii) repair vs. regression trade-offs, and
(iii) trajectory sensitivity of the R-path on borderline hard instances.
Therefore, we report not only hard recall but also the S/R counterfactual matrices to make the cost–fidelity behavior transparent.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Router Error Analysis and Failure Modes</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We analyze routing errors relative, clustered into coherent categories (Table <a href="#A5.T15" title="Table 15 ‣ False cache misses dominate and reflect conservative bias. ‣ Appendix E Router Error Analysis and Failure Modes ‣ From Lossy to Verified: A Provenance-Aware Tiered Memory for Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>).
We distinguish two asymmetric error types:
<span id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(i) S<math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>R errors</span> (false cache hits), where the router answers from Tier-1 but raw grounding is required; and
<span id="A5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(ii) R<math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>S errors</span> (false cache misses), where the router escalates unnecessarily despite sufficient summary evidence.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">False cache hits are rarer but more harmful.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">S<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>R errors are relatively rare (61 cases) but directly impact correctness.
They stem mainly from <em id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">information completeness</em> failures (missing a required slot such as an entity name) and <em id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">precision requirement</em> failures (ignoring that the question demands exactness or attribution).
These cases align with known brittleness of lossy compression: a summary can be topically relevant yet underspecified for exact answering.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">False cache misses dominate and reflect conservative bias.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">R<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>S errors are much more frequent (371 cases).
The primary cause is <em id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">false information gap detection</em>: the router assumes summaries are insufficient even when they contain enough evidence.
These errors increase cost but typically do not degrade correctness, reflecting a conservative policy that prioritizes faithfulness.
This suggests a clear path for future improvement: better calibration and sufficiency detection that leverages indirect but adequate evidence while still avoiding false cache hits.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.T15" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A5.T15.3" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A5.T15.3.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A5.T15.3.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt"><span id="A5.T15.3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Error Category</span></th>
<td id="A5.T15.3.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt"><span id="A5.T15.3.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Count</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A5.T15.3.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A5.T15.3.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t" colspan="2"><span id="A5.T15.3.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">S<math id="A5.T15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>R Errors (Summary insufficient, escalation needed)</span></th></tr>
<tr id="A5.T15.3.3" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A5.T15.3.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t"><span id="A5.T15.3.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Information completeness error</span></th>
<td id="A5.T15.3.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t"><span id="A5.T15.3.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">26</span></td></tr>

<td id="A5.T15.3.13.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><span id="A5.T15.3.13.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">371</span></td></tr>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 15: </span><span id="A5.T15.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Router error analysis.</span>
We categorize routing errors into false cache hits (S<math id="A5.T15.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>R) and false cache misses (R<math id="A5.T15.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>S).
False cache hits are relatively rare but stem mainly from summary incompleteness and unmet precision requirements.
False cache misses dominate and primarily reflect conservative over-escalation, incurring additional cost without affecting correctness.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Prompts Used in the TierMem System</h2>

<figure id="A6.F4" class="ltx_figure"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A6.F4.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="783.76" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 477.38 783.76" 5.91 1.97 C 3.73 1.97 1.97 3.73 1.97 5.91 Z"></path></g><g transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 15 760.08)"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" class="ltx_nestedsvg" style="--ltx-fo-width:18.03em;--ltx-fo-height:0.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="13.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 10.38)" width="249.53"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="A6.F4.pic1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Fact Extraction Prompt (JSON Schema)</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.55)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:36.91em;--ltx-fo-height:53.03em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.2em;font-size:10pt;" height="736.57" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 733.8)" width="510.73"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.91em;">
<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are the <span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Universal Memory Encoder</span>. Your goal is to convert raw input stream into high-fidelity, self-contained knowledge records (Long-term Memory).</span></span>
<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">INPUT FORMATTING NOTICE: 
<br class="ltx_break">The input will be provided in the next user message, prefixed by ‘Input:’ and often formatted as dialogue lines. 
<br class="ltx_break">It may follow a pattern like: ‘[Timestamp] Speaker_Name: Content’.</span></span>
<span id="A6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If this pattern is present, you MUST use the ‘Timestamp’ for temporal grounding and ‘Speaker_Name’ for entity resolution.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If this pattern is absent (e.g., raw document text), treat the input as a factual source and extract knowledge propositions.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">CORE OBJECTIVES:<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<span id="A6.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="A6.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ENTITY &amp; CONTEXT RESOLUTION</span><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">:</span></span>
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">No ambiguous references</span><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Every extracted fact must explicitly name the involved people, organizations, objects, places, and concepts.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">No “User” ambiguity</span><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: If the input says ‘[… ] Melanie: I like art’, the fact MUST be “Melanie likes art”, NOT “The user likes art”.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">De-contextualization</span><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Each extracted fact must be </span><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">standalone</span><span id="A6.I2.i1.I1.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="A6.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">TEMPORAL GROUNDING</span><span id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Use the provided timestamps in the input as the source of truth. Convert relative time (“tomorrow”, “next week”) into absolute context.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="A6.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">PRONOUN &amp; DEIXIS ELIMINATION</span><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Extracted facts must </span><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">not contain any pronouns</span><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. If a pronoun appears, resolve it to the specific entity.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="A6.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SCENE TAGGING (EMBEDDED)</span><span id="A6.I2.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Identify the immediate scene/activity (2-5 words). Append this scene to the end of the fact string inside brackets.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS (MUST FOLLOW):<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 
<br class="ltx_break">Return a JSON object with EXACTLY this schema:</span></span></span><pre id="A6.F4.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
{
  "facts": [
      "&lt;atomic fact sentence 1&gt; [Scene: ...]",
      "&lt;atomic fact sentence 2&gt; [Scene: ...]", ...
  ]
}
</pre>
<span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F4.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Rules: Output JSON only (no extra text, no markdown code fences).</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A6.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="A6.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The prompt used for extracting atomic facts from conversation streams.</span></figcaption>
</figure>

Prompt</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.24)"><foreignObject class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:36.91em;">
<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are a research assistant extracting facts from conversation evidence to answer a question.</span></span>
<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">QUESTION:<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {question} 
<br class="ltx_break"></span>RETRIEVED EVIDENCE:<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {evidence}</span></span></span>
<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">YOUR TASK:<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 
<br class="ltx_break">Read through ALL pages in the evidence and extract facts that help answer the question.</span></span></span>
<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">EXTRACTION STRATEGY:<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 
<br class="ltx_break">Identify what information is needed and extract:</span></span></span>
<span id="A6.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<span id="A6.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="A6.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Direct answers</span><span id="A6.I3.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Facts that directly answer the question</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="A6.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Component facts</span><span id="A6.I3.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Facts about entities/topics in the question that can be combined</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="A6.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Temporal facts</span><span id="A6.I3.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: When events happened</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="A6.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Confirmation facts</span><span id="A6.I3.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Look for acceptance/approval messages</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">OUTPUT FORMAT (JSON):<span id="A6.F5.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span><pre id="A6.F5.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
{
  "linked_facts": [
    {
      "fact": "&lt;extracted fact - use specific dates/names&gt;",
      "evidence_quote": "&lt;EXACT quote from the evidence&gt;"
    }
  ],
  "coverage_assessment": "&lt;what aspects are covered vs missing&gt;"
}
</pre>

<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">QUESTION:<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> {question}

<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">YOUR TASK:<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 
<br class="ltx_break">Decide whether the current facts are SUFFICIENT to answer the question, or if more search is needed.</span></span></span>
<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">OUTPUT FORMAT (JSON):<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span><pre id="A6.F6.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
{
  "decision": "DONE" or "SEARCH",
  "reasoning": "&lt;brief explanation&gt;",
  "search_commands": [
    {"type": "MEM0_SEARCH", "query": "&lt;semantic search query&gt;"},

<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">DECISION CRITERIA:<span id="A6.F6.pic1.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>

<span id="A6.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">DONE</span><span id="A6.I4.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: The facts contain enough information to provide a reasonable answer.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span>

<span id="A6.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SEARCH</span><span id="A6.I4.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Key information is missing and more search might help.</span></span>

<span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are an expert router for a memory-augmented QA system. Analyze the retrieved summaries and decide the best action to answer the question.</span></span>
<span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Available actions:<span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 
<br class="ltx_break">1. ”S” - Answer using current summaries only. Use when Summaries contain the EXPLICIT answer.

<span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Question: {q}

<span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F7.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output format (JSON only):</span></span><pre id="A6.F7.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
- If answering with summaries: {"action": "S"}
- If deep research needed: {"action": "R"}

330.23 0 328.6 0 L 2.95 0 C 1.32 0 0 1.32 0 2.95 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 11.81 8.38)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:22.45em;--ltx-fo-height:0.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="13.84" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 10.38)" width="310.63"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="A6.F8.pic1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">Answer Generation Prompts (Template Functions)</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 21.65 16.24)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:31.37em;--ltx-fo-height:13.76em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.18em;font-size:10pt;" class="ltx_minipage" height="192.8" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 190.34)" width="36.91em"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><pre id="A6.F8.pic1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">def _make_locomo_summary_prompt(summary: str, question: str) -&gt; str:
    return f"""\
Based on the summary below, write an answer in the form of **a short phrase**...
Answer with exact words from the context whenever possible.
For date/time, strictly follow the format "15 July 2023"...

QUESTION: {question}
SUMMARY: {summary}
Short answer:
"""

def _make_longmemeval_prompt(summary: str, question: str) -&gt; str:
    return f"""\
You are an intelligent memory assistant tasked with retrieving accurate
information from episodic memories.

# INSTRUCTIONS:
Synthesize information from different memories to answer the user’s question.
It is CRITICAL that you move beyond simple fact extraction and perform
logical inference. Answer the question in a short phrase.

QUESTION: {question}
SUMMARY: {summary}
Short answer:
"""
</pre></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>

<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are a strict quality judge for memory facts. Given a question and candidate facts, select ONLY high-quality facts that meet ALL criteria.</span></span>
<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Question: {question} 
<br class="ltx_break">Candidate Facts: {facts_list}</span></span>
<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Quality Criteria (ALL must be met):<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.I5" class="ltx_enumerate">
<span id="A6.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<span id="A6.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Directly Relevant</span><span id="A6.I5.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Directly helps answer this specific question.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<span id="A6.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I5.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Specific &amp; Concrete</span><span id="A6.I5.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Contains names, dates, numbers, locations.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<span id="A6.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I5.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I5.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Factually Grounded</span><span id="A6.I5.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">: Based on concrete conversation content.</span></span>
</span></span>
<span id="A6.I5.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<span id="A6.I5.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<span id="A6.I5.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I5.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Non-redundant</span><span id="A6.I5.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> &amp; </span><span id="A6.I5.i4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Self-contained</span><span id="A6.I5.i4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></span>
</span></span>
</span>
<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Reject facts that are:<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Too general, obvious from the question, vague, or tangentially related.</span></span></span>
<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Output format:<span id="A6.F9.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Return ONLY a JSON array of selected fact indices (0-based), e.g., [0, 2], [1], or [] if none qualify.</span></span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>

<span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Your task is to label an answer to a question as ‘CORRECT’ or ‘WRONG’.
You will be given:
(1) a question (posed by one user to another user),
(2) a ‘gold’ (ground truth) answer,
(3) a generated answer.</span></span>
<span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The gold answer will usually be a concise and short answer.
The generated answer might be much longer, but you should be generous
with your grading - as long as it touches on the same topic/time
as the gold answer, it should be counted as CORRECT.</span></span>
<span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Question: {question}
Gold answer: {gold_answer}
Generated answer: {generated_answer}</span></span>
<span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.F10.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">First, provide a short (one sentence) explanation of your reasoning,
then finish with CORRECT or WRONG in a json format with the key as ”label”.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A6.F10.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A6.F10.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">The LLM-as-a-Judge prompt used for automated evaluation.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
